properties.value: Grouping is dominated by a regex artifact — the 'dsa' pattern matching inside 'ecdsa': most of the 408 sites are ECDSA-P256 key-generation op-chains already carried by the ECDSA (ALG-710f61f0) and P-256 (ALG-92e838c9) objects. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production RSA: the CA requires RSA issuers alongside ECDSA (ca/ca.go:180) and signs certificates with RSA for RSA hierarchies; the ACME WFE accepts RSA account keys and verifies RS256 JWS signatures; the ceremony tool generates RSA root/intermediate keys inside an HSM via PKCS#11 with the modulus taken from ceremony config (2048/3072/4096 enforced per cmd/ceremony tests; 1024 rejected). Most of the 120 sites are 2048-bit test-keygen fixtures plus key-type switches. RSA is used for signing here,

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Self-signed certificate constructions: overwhelmingly unit-test fixtures (ca, ceremony, admin, crl tests create self-signed certs to exercise signing paths). The legitimate production use is the key ceremony creating self-signed ROOT CA certificates (cmd/ceremony), where self-signing is the definition of a root. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Heuristic "non-constant-time comparison" sites. The security-relevant subset is empty in production code: the only constant-time-sensitive comparisons (bearer/api tokens in test/salesforce-test-srv, test/zendesk-test-srv) live in test-double servers; production digest comparisons (cmd/cert-checker/main.go:365 compares a stored SHA-256 fingerprint of public certificate data) are consistency checks, not secret-dependent; several sites are nil/empty checks (sa/saro.go:707, pardot.go:106) or test as

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: math/rand/v2 (non-cryptographic PRNG) imports. Every actual use is non-security: retry-backoff jitter (core/util.go:453), random issuer-pool selection (ca/ca.go:481), random CT-log choice (ctpolicy/loglist), DNS resolver rotation (bdns), gRPC backoff, and test fixtures generating throwaway IDs. Production randomness for certificate serials and keys uses crypto/rand, not this. Weak-RNG rule fires on the import; no security-relevant consumption found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWS algorithm test vectors for the ACME WFE verifier: RS256 (RSA-PKCS1v15 + SHA-256) and PS256 (RSA-PSS + SHA-256) are production-supported account-key algorithms — the WFE verifies RS256/PS256 signatures on every ACME request carrying an RSA account key. The sites themselves are unit-test fixtures (TestCheckAlgorithm and JWS bodies) exercising that supported path. Quantum-vulnerable RSA signing on the public API surface — migration ML-DSA (or hybrid) for ACME account keys. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Negative tests: TestRejectsHS256 (and its case table) construct HS256 JWS bodies to assert that the WFE's supported-algorithm list — which admits only asymmetric algorithms — REJECTS symmetric JWTs. HS256 is not accepted anywhere in production; these fixtures exist to prove the rejection. Recorded posture control, not an accepted algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Core CA signing algorithm. Production posture: the certificate authority refuses to start unless an ECDSA issuer is configured (ca/ca.go:180 requires both ECDSA and RSA issuers) and signs leaf/pre-certificates with ECDSA (P-256/P-384 per issuance profile); the ceremony tool generates ECDSA root/intermediate keys inside an HSM via PKCS#11 (cmd/ceremony/key.go ecGenerate, curve from ceremony config, P-256/P-384/P-521 accepted); ACME account keys in JWS ES256 also rely on ECDSA. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve-level view of the ECDSA inventory: secp256r1 (P-256) is the default curve for the CA's ECDSA issuance profiles and appears throughout as ecdsa.GenerateKey(elliptic.P256(), ...) in ceremony/admin/wfe/ra test fixtures and profile configuration. Quantum-vulnerable curve (Shor) — the P-256 discrete log breaks with a CRQC. Overlaps the ECDSA object (ALG-710f61f0); kept as the curve-tagged CBOM entry. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All Go crypto/tls session setups in the tree (internal mTLS mesh via cmd/config.go, DNS-over-TLS client in bdns, WFE/gRPC servers, test servers) on the tree's Go 1.27.0 toolchain. Go 1.24+ enables the hybrid post-quantum X25519MLKEM768 key exchange by default for TLS 1.3, so these sessions negotiate PQ KEX against any capable peer unless parameters are pinned down — the only pins found are TLS 1.3 (internal mesh, cmd/config.go:224, which keeps PQ defaults) and TLS 1.2 minimum on the VA validatio

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 appears only in test fixtures: CA/linter/issuance unit tests and the cosignature-tree tests (trees/cosignature), including one hardcoded test seed at linter_test.go:50. It is not in the production issuance path (the CA issues ECDSA/RSA/ML-DSA). Recorded because the test corpus exercises the algorithm and the linter must handle Ed25519 certificates; quantum-vulnerable signature family if ever promoted to production use. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWS algorithm test vectors: ES256 (ECDSA P-256) and ES512 (ECDSA P-521) are production-supported ACME account-key algorithms — the WFE's supported-algorithm list admits them and verifies such signatures on requests. These sites are the unit-test fixtures exercising that path. Quantum-vulnerable ECDSA on the public API surface — same migration story as the CA's ECDSA signing (ML-DSA). Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Test Redis pins tls-protocols to "TLSv1.3" only — no TLS 1.2 negotiation is possible. Key-exchange groups depend on the Redis/OpenSSL build underneath (not pinned here); a Redis built on a PQ-capable OpenSSL could offer hybrid groups. Protocol-configuration asset, test scope, replaceable only by the vendor's TLS stack.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Production CA key generation: cmd/ceremony/ecdsa.go maps P-384/P-521 (and P-256) curve names to curves and their ASN.1 OIDs for keys generated inside an HSM via PKCS#11; cmd/ceremony/main.go:124 pins the allowed-curve policy ("P-384": true). P-384/P-521 ECDSA keys are the strongest ECDSA hierarchies this CA can deploy — still quantum-vulnerable (Shor breaks the ECDLP on all NIST curves). Migration ML-DSA. Changeable in software; deployed hierarchies long-lived observables.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Boulder's post-quantum migration is already landing: crypto/mldsa (Go stdlib ML-DSA, FIPS 204). The issuance stack classifies ML-DSA issuer keys — issuance/issuer.go:284 returns x509.MLDSA / x509.MLDSA44 for *mldsa.PublicKey — and cmd/boulder-mtpublisher verifies the CA certificate's ML-DSA public key (main.go:119) and the mirror's ML-DSA public key from file (main.go:124) for Merkle-tree publishing. Parameter set in use is ML-DSA-44; ML-DSA-65/87 are the higher security categories for productio

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 throughout the production CA: JWK/account-key digests, subject-key identifiers and SPKI hashes (core/util.go:136/156/202), CRL hashing (ca/crl.go:158), certificate fingerprints, bs3 test corpus. Grover halves the classical margin but SHA-256 remains acceptable and is the hash paired with every signature algorithm in use; no migration pressure. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Sunlight (Merkle-tree CT log) test key generator: HKDF-SHA256 (crypto/hkdf) derives a 32-byte mirror secret from a seed with the info label "sunlight ML-DSA-44 mirror key" — deterministic generation of the ML-DSA-44 mirror keys used by the sunlight/mtpublisher test deployment. Test tooling only; KDF output feeds the PQ (ML-DSA) signing path, not a legacy primitive. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 capability enters the build through declared dependencies: golang.org/x/crypto (per the go.mod comment about a sub-package), Go 1.27's stdlib crypto/pbkdf2, and go-jose/v4's PBES2 JWE path in vendored source. No Boulder application code invokes PBKDF2 — the ACME WFE handles JWS only, never password-based JWE. Available in the shipped libraries; no application call site found. Dependency-inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X.509 handling is this codebase's product surface: a CA that parses, creates, signs, and verifies certificates throughout (parsing stored certs in ca/, PEM trust pools for DNS-over-TLS roots in bdns/, re-verification in cert-checker, JWS certificate handling in wfe2/). Confirmed as a class — the X.509 machinery is the PKI asset; the algorithm-level posture is carried separately by the ECDSA/RSA/DSA/ML-DSA objects. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto/rand (OS CSPRNG) is the randomness source for everything security-relevant: certificate serial generation (ca/ca.go:491 rand.Read, with an explicit comment on Go 1.24+ guarantees), all key generation, JWS anti-replay nonces, and test fixtures. Not quantum-relevant; secure by construction in Go. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: CSRs are the CA's intake surface: the csr/ package parses and signature-verifies applicant CertificateRequests before issuance, and ca/testdata/testcsr.go generates fixture CSRs (ECDSA and others). Most of the 21 sites are test fixtures constructing CSRs via x509.CreateCertificateRequest; cmd/ceremony/cert.go:349 is an error-path test with a failReader. PKI-object handling, changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: filippo.io/edwards25519: the curve-arithmetic library underlying Ed25519 signature handling, reached via the JOSE/EdDSA dependency chain; no direct Boulder call site. Ed25519 is quantum-vulnerable as a signature family, but Boulder's own Ed25519 usage is test-only (see the Ed25519 object). Library-surface inventory entry.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: go-jose/v4 v4.1.5 is the production ACME JOSE library: the WFE parses and verifies every ACME request's JWS with it (RS256/PS256/ES256/ES512/EdDSA per the supported-algs list). The vendored copy also ships JWE/PBES2 (PBKDF2) capability that Boulder never calls. Its RSA/ECDSA verification paths are the quantum-vulnerable signature-verification surface of the public ACME API. Changeable here (version pin in go.mod).

properties.name: pqs:context

No credential values are hardcoded here; the types carry runtime-provided credentials from the environment/instance role. Observable here; replaceable only by the vendor (AWS SDK).
